claims.claim: Under the Wagner-Whitin condition, physical path costs differ from reduced arc costs K_i + q_i(D_j-D_i) only by a path-independent term, and ordered slopes imply Monge arcs.
claims.scope: Deterministic single-item uncapacitated model with ordered reduced slopes.

claims.claim: The weighted-infinity distance, with coordinate demand floors, to a tie against one fixed path is given by the coordinate-separable formula in Theorem 5.1.
claims.scope: A fixed outside path and fixed comparator; finite rational input in the theorem.
claims.uncertainty: Certified through the exact rational layer (wwprefix.exactcert); every finite radius carries an exactly verified tie witness. No proof-assistant formalisation.

claims.claim: The prefix-deviation directed acyclic graph maps source-sink paths bijectively to complete paths that leave the protected prefix.
claims.scope: Selected complete nominal path and k protected arcs.
claims.uncertainty: Computational enumeration is finite and producer-side.

claims.claim: The frozen-comparator prefix radius is computable by at most T+1 shortest-path calculations and polynomial-size Charnes-Cooper linear programmes.
claims.scope: Ordered-slope Wagner-Whitin model, weighted infinity ball, demand floors.
claims.uncertainty: Polynomial bit complexity, not a strongly polynomial claim. The released certification computes the same value in exact rational arithmetic (breakpoint binary search plus parametric shortest paths); the Charnes-Cooper LP remains the proof device and the floating diagnostic path only.

claims.claim: The frozen radius is a valid lower bound, an exposed outside path yields a feasible inverse-LP upper bound, and a closing witness or coincident bounds certifies the exact strong radius.
claims.uncertainty: A non-closed bracket is genuinely unresolved; both certified ends are witness-backed in exact arithmetic.

claims.claim: A positive-floor three-period instance has frozen radius 1.5 and exact strong prefix radius 2.0.
Each fixed outside competitor has a compact inverse shortest-path linear programme; the exact radius is their finite disjunction; fixed-radius decision has an O(T^3)-size mixed-integer formulation.
claims.scope: Finite horizon and bounded demand box induced by a proposed radius for the MILP.
claims.uncertainty: No polynomial-time exact algorithm or hardness result for the demand-induced restriction; generic partial inverse and anti-inverse shortest paths are NP-hard (Gassner 2009; Ley and Merkert 2025). Candidate generation is exponential. Escalation results are certified: point-exact or explicit certified intervals.

claims.claim: Floor-aware split-conformal scoring gives one-step marginal coverage under exchangeability, and a prespecified finite family can use Bonferroni allocation.
claims.scope: Exchangeable calibration and next score; prespecified scoring and admissibility rule.
claims.uncertainty: No conditional, adaptive, time-uniform or distribution-shift guarantee.

claims.claim: Bellman residuals telescope and ordered slopes yield a deterministic structural-loss bound with a dead zone equal to the certified prefix radius.
claims.scope: Admissible realised demand, structural setup commitments, uncapacitated quantity recourse and disclosed cycle-boundary replanning.
claims.uncertainty: Does not cover fixed quantities, capacities, transport slots or service loss.

claims.claim: The end-to-end interface can be applied retrospectively to an observed demand series with reconstructed vintages and stylised costs, returning bounded commitment decisions and unresolved states.
claims.scope: The frozen 60-row UCI demand data and the disclosed reconstruction, not the source organisation's historical planning system.
claims.uncertainty: Not field validation; forecasts, costs and counterfactual policies are reconstructed.

claims.claim: The candidate novel object is prefix-face stability with a moving best inside continuation, not demand-vector stability or fixed-solution sensitivity in general.
claims.scope: Bounded literature search frozen 5 August 2026; inspected-copy hashes retained without redistributing article full text.
claims.uncertainty: No lawful digital copy of Richter and Voros (1989) exists (DOI test-prefix stub only; the 1987-94 EIK run was never digitised). Bibliography corrected; zbMATH review (Zbl 0672.90033) triangulated: fixed-solution stability regions, joint case a two-parameter region, no indication of a prefix-class object. Theorem-level overlap remains unresolved pending print acquisition (routes documented in docs/literature_audit.md).

claims.claim: Every value published under a certified_* key is computed, or a posteriori verified, in exact rational arithmetic with zero tolerances; floating point participates only as a search heuristic whose proposals are exactly re-verified; infinite radii are published only with structural or saturation proofs.
claims.uncertainty: The trusted base is the exact layer plus a separately implemented producer-side checker; neither is proof-assistant verified or organisationally independent. For T>12 frozen-minimality relies on internally cross-checked parametric computation.

claims.claim: The peer-review false-infinity counterexample (review 4.1) is certified correctly: under exact decimal semantics the radius is exactly 1 and a proposed radius of 1.1 is classified certified_destabilising_witness_exists; under binary-float semantics the exact radius of the instance actually supplied is approximately 1.0000000283 with the same classification.

Rescalings of cost units and demand units (with q and weights transformed accordingly) never flip a certificate between finite and infinite and never reverse a triage classification. Unconditional when the rescaling is performed in exact rational arithmetic; for rescalings performed in binary floating point the guarantee holds in the absence of underflow or overflow while forming the rescaled inputs (Sol adversarial review, finding 8).
claims.proof: Exact arithmetic; asserted as a hard invariant in the audit.
claims.scope: Audited rescaling grid; property holds by construction for all exact inputs.
claims.uncertainty: Binary-performed rescalings near the subnormal or overflow range alter the instance itself before ingestion; exact decimal/rational strings avoid this entirely. Non-power-of-two decimal rescalings likewise change the binary instance.

claims.claim: scripts/check_certificate.py re-verifies decision records from first principles without importing the package: nominal optimality, witnesses, floors, distances, exact ties, inside domination, saturation-infinity proofs and triage logic; for T<=12 it re-derives frozen minimality by complete enumeration.
claims.uncertainty: This is separately implemented producer-side checking, not organisationally independent reproduction. Checker and package share Python and its integer arithmetic.

global_limitations: No independent clean-room reproduction of the full pipeline (the shipped producer-side checker separately re-verifies decision records).
No field validation or demonstrated industrial effect.
Certified values are exact-rational; floating point remains in search, diagnostics and the MILP escalation, whose negative answers are solver-level only.
Exact computational complexity of the demand-induced restriction remains open; generic partial inverse analogues are NP-hard.
